feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, credible progression, and relevant digital strategy depth. It reads professionally and is well structured, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director and consultant roles; this supports credibility and leadership growth.  
- Strong domain alignment for digital communications/strategy roles, with solid coverage of web, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and governance.  
- Writing is generally polished and concise, with good use of action verbs and concrete platform references (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI).

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes. Include measurable gains in engagement, efficiency, adoption, conversions, email performance, or production savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve scannability and make the CV feel tighter.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; add the serial comma consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” is inconsistent with other lines); “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that reflect the most recent enterprise-level work.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” and lead with the current value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a tighter summary of enterprise, cross-channel leadership.
- Add context from recent roles, such as mission-driven/member organizations, digital transformation, or large-scale web/content ecosystems.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in web strategy, editorial workflow design, email and social programs, multimedia production, and analytics-enabled decision-making. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear content, aligning stakeholders, and building scalable systems that improve execution across complex teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” repeat heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is already reinforced throughout NACo experience, so keep it brief here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “Digital platform modernization,” “Editorial systems & governance.”
- Group related items to reduce list sprawl and improve scanability; suggested version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web operations & CMS administration • Editorial systems, workflow design & governance • Analytics, reporting & performance insights • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; change “communication” to “communications” for consistency.
- Prioritize strategic capabilities over lower-level operational ones unless targeting hands-on digital roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, multi-channel communications, analytics, stakeholder coordination, and multimedia.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” is close to “Editorial workflow design” and may be redundant.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a broad service list. Tighten it around highest-value consulting outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory/consulting scope, platform builds, and AI search leadership.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/properties supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow improvements, search accuracy/engagement gains, or time saved.
- Example rewrite: “Led development of AI-enabled search, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital strategy, content operations, governance, workflows” overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 Director role; keep this entry focused on consulting deliverables completed since Oct. 2024.
- Microsites, AI search, and campaigns also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization bullet and make it more outcome-driven: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page Drupal website, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten channel-management language and add performance metrics if available: email open/click growth, social engagement, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Combine operations/governance/analytics into one concise bullet emphasizing decision-making and efficiency: “Built reporting and governance systems across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving visibility, publishing consistency, and cross-team planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed here as building the in-house studio/capability.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + level: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around launch/growth: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and execution.” Add metrics if possible (open rates, production volume, turnaround time, audience growth).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social and video” is very similar to the Director role; keep this entry more execution-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this role as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline item should emphasize higher-value, recent platform leadership and implementation strengths rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing tied to recent work: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or older items unless central to target roles; consider dropping “WordPress,” “SharePoint,” “Power Pages,” and “jQuery” from this topline line.
- Use “front-end implementation” instead of listing every language here; keep detailed stack in “Technical + IT.”
- If space allows, sharpen impact orientation: “Enterprise Drupal delivery” or “Large-scale CMS modernization” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic and save full platform/tool lists for the technical section.

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be trimmed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add proficiency cues tied to recent work: “Drupal 9/10” or “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 50+ publishers)” to reinforce impact.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels lighter than the rest of the stack.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV: use either “CMS platforms” or “Web Platforms & CMS” across sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2]; consider removing one version or making this section more technical/specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and modern tools most relevant to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & Technical Implementation:** HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier instead of more tools, e.g., “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “deployment automation,” or “serverless scripting” to show applied use.
- Order by strength/relevance: JavaScript • API integrations • GTM • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML/CSS

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if you want this section to signal hands-on technical execution.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation,” “Airtable systems,” and cross-functional planning already emphasized in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function and tighten wording: “Automation & Workflow: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier” and move Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello to a separate “Project & Work Management” line.
- Remove Slack and Teams from this item unless collaboration tools are listed consistently elsewhere; they dilute the automation focus.
- Consider a more impact-oriented label: “Workflow Automation & Work Management.”
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers in a summary section instead of here, e.g., “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable/Power Automate” or “supported editorial planning across 50+ publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same emphasis here without added specificity.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello echo planning/governance themes already covered in recent NACo roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it reads as a generic tool list. Strengthen it by signaling enterprise-scale email/engagement capability and aligning terminology with the rest of the CV.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope-oriented wording elsewhere in this section or adjacent skills, e.g. **enterprise email automation**, **newsletter operations**, or **member engagement platforms**
- Use the most current product naming consistently: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** rather than a slash format

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating audience scale here unless you add a distinct systems/automation angle.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than strategic.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, email/social performance, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on production and publishing workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” and workflow improvement overlap with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as the launch/foundation stage.
- Avoid broad channel lists if no outcomes are added; later roles already cover enterprise oversight.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator

- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the second sentence stronger and more concise: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.
- Consider replacing “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb/result, e.g., “produced multimedia assets for program and policy communications.”

- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing that repeats later digital/media roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later entries already show progression into management.
